title: Maximum Twin Sum of a Linked List
summary: Given an even-sized linked list, find the highest twin sum where the twin of the i-th node is the (n-1-i)-th node, and n is the list's size.
statement: Given an even-sized linked list, find the highest twin sum where the twin of the i-th node is the (n-1-i)-th node, and n is the list's size. For example, in a list of four nodes, the twin sum of node 0 with node 3 and node 1 with node 2 are calculated to find the maximum.
constraints: The linked list has positive even length.
Node i is paired with node n-1-i; calculate each pair once.
Return the maximum twin sum without changing node values.
hints: Twin positions are symmetric around the list endpoints.
Collect values once, then compare values[i]+values[n-1-i] over the first half.
Return max(values[i]+values[-1-i] for i in range(n//2)).
Every node belongs to exactly one symmetric pair, and first-half indices enumerate all pairs without duplication.
editorial: Every node belongs to exactly one symmetric pair, and first-half indices enumerate all pairs without duplication.

tests.explanation: Twin pairs sum to six and six, so the maximum is six.
The outer nodes sum to seven, exceeding the inner sum four.
